correctness.rationale: An independent integer-only enumeration exhausted all 1, 16, and 19,683 operation tables on the carriers of sizes 1, 2, and 3. It tested M by equality of its left-translation row with the diagonal, and B by L_{(B·x)·y}=L_x∘L_y for every x,y, computing associativity by L_{x·y}=L_x∘L_y. It formed full marked permutation orbits and computed closure of the marks. The resulting tuples (labelled, marked classes, generated classes, nonassociative classes, generated nonassociative classes) were (1,1,1,0,0), (14,7,4,0,0), and (204,36,7,6,1). At order 3 the six specified nonassociative representatives have disjoint size-six marked orbits; the underlying types are distinct (they have one versus two nonzero products relative to the unique absorbing element). The fixed counts are 204,4,4,4,0,0. Only the marking B=0,M=2 of Type II generates its carrier, because 2·2=1. The explicit associativity failure follows by the two products displayed in the finding.
residual_risks: Exhaustiveness is confined to orders 1–3, and counts marked structures with possibly coincident marks. The replay is not formal verification.

value.rationale: The census locates the first failure of associativity after relaxing the identity-bearing BI setting and distinguishes arbitrary markings from generation by the named combinators. For a researcher looking for smallest BM witnesses, the six-class list establishes which alternatives exist, and the uniqueness result identifies the only generated obstruction at the cutoff. This is a natural finite classification, not merely a replay of the famous or already displayed example.
residual_risks: No larger-order classification or novelty of the underlying search algorithm is credited.
